items.title: Nutrition & deficiency diseases
items.body:
A **balanced diet** supplies **macronutrients** (carbohydrates and fats for energy, proteins for growth/repair) and **micronutrients** (vitamins and minerals in small amounts). Fats give ~9 kcal/g versus ~4 kcal/g for carbohydrates and proteins.

**Deficiency diseases** are a favourite exam area:

| Nutrient lacking | Disease / sign |
|---|---|
| Vitamin A | Night blindness, xerophthalmia |
| Vitamin B1 (thiamine) | Beriberi |
| Vitamin B3 (niacin) | Pellagra (dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia) |
| Vitamin C | Scurvy (bleeding gums) |
| Vitamin D | Rickets (children), osteomalacia (adults) |
| Iodine | Goitre, cretinism |
| Iron | Anaemia |

**Protein-energy malnutrition:** **kwashiorkor** (protein deficiency with oedema, distended belly) and **marasmus** (severe energy + protein deficit with wasting).
keyPoints: Macronutrients = carbohydrates, proteins, fats; micronutrients = vitamins, minerals.
Fats yield ~9 kcal/g; carbohydrates and proteins ~4 kcal/g each.
Scurvy = Vitamin C; rickets = Vitamin D; beriberi = B1; pellagra = B3 (niacin).
Goitre = iodine deficiency; anaemia = iron deficiency; night blindness = Vitamin A.
Kwashiorkor = protein deficiency (oedema); marasmus = energy + protein deficit (wasting).
items.source: NCERT Science; ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition

items.title: Communicable, vector-borne & non-communicable diseases
items.body:
**Communicable diseases** spread via pathogens. Classify by pathogen type:
- **Bacterial:** tuberculosis (airborne, *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*), cholera (water/food, *Vibrio cholerae*), plague.
- **Viral:** dengue, COVID-19, H1N1 (swine flu), Nipah (fruit-bat reservoir), Japanese encephalitis.
- **Protozoan:** malaria (*Plasmodium*), kala-azar (*Leishmania*).

**Vector-borne pathogen–vector pairs (high-yield):**

| Disease | Pathogen | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| Malaria | Plasmodium (protozoan) | Female Anopheles |
| Dengue/Chikungunya/Zika | Virus | Aedes aegypti |
| Lymphatic filariasis | Wuchereria (worm) | Culex |
| Japanese encephalitis | Virus | Culex |
| Kala-azar | Leishmania | Sandfly (Phlebotomus) |

**Non-communicable diseases (NCDs)** — diabetes, hypertension, cancer, cardiovascular disease — are non-infectious, driven by tobacco, alcohol, poor diet and inactivity, and now cause the majority of deaths in India (addressed by NP-NCD screening).
keyPoints: Bacterial: TB (airborne), cholera (water/food); Viral: dengue, COVID-19, Nipah, JE; Protozoan: malaria, kala-azar.
Malaria → Anopheles; Dengue/Chikungunya → Aedes; Filariasis & JE → Culex; Kala-azar → Sandfly.
Nipah virus reservoir = fruit bats (Pteropus); outbreaks mainly in Kerala.
NCDs (diabetes, hypertension, cancer, CVD) are non-infectious and lifestyle-linked.
NCDs cause the majority of deaths in India; NP-NCD runs population-based screening.

items.title: Immunity, vaccines & the Universal Immunization Programme
items.body:
**Immunity** types:
- **Active** — body makes its own antibodies after infection or vaccination; durable (memory cells).
- **Passive** — ready-made antibodies received (mother's milk, antiserum); immediate but short-lived.
- **Herd immunity** — when a large share of the population is immune, spread slows, protecting the unvaccinated.

**Vaccines** contain weakened (attenuated), killed, or subunit parts of a pathogen to train memory cells.

**Universal Immunization Programme (UIP), 1985** — one of the world's largest, now protecting against **12 diseases** (TB, diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, polio, measles, rubella, hepatitis B, rotavirus, Japanese encephalitis, pneumonia/pneumococcal). Hepatitis B was added in 2007 and PCV in 2017.

**Mission Indradhanush (2014)** and Intensified MI (2017) target unvaccinated/partially vaccinated children and pregnant women; **U-WIN** is the digital registry (CoWIN-model) to record and track every dose.
keyPoints: Active immunity = self-made antibodies (durable); passive = ready-made antibodies (immediate, short-lived).
Herd immunity protects the unvaccinated when enough people are immune.
UIP launched 1985; free vaccines against 12 diseases.
Hepatitis B added to UIP in 2007; pneumococcal (PCV) in 2017.
Mission Indradhanush (2014) raises full-immunization coverage; U-WIN digitally tracks vaccinations.

items.title: Health missions — Ayushman Bharat, ABDM & NHM
items.body:
**Ayushman Bharat (2018)** has two pillars:
1. **PM-JAY** — health cover of **₹5 lakh per family per year** for secondary/tertiary care; world's largest health assurance scheme; targets the poorest ~40% (SECC data).
2. **Ayushman Arogya Mandir** (formerly Health & Wellness Centres) — comprehensive primary care.

**Ayushman Vay Vandana (2024)** extends free ₹5 lakh cover to **all citizens aged 70+**, regardless of income.

**Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM, 2021)** issues the 14-digit **ABHA** health ID linking digital health records.

**National Health Mission (NHM)** = **NRHM (2005)** + **NUHM (2013)**; front-line **ASHA** workers are its backbone. The **National Health Policy 2017** targets public health spending of **2.5% of GDP** (from ~1.2%). Related: **Tele-MANAS (2022)** for mental health under NMHP (1982); AP runs **Dr NTR Vaidya Seva (Aarogyasri)**.
keyPoints: Ayushman Bharat (2018) = PM-JAY (₹5 lakh cover) + Ayushman Arogya Mandir (HWCs).
Ayushman Vay Vandana (2024) covers all citizens aged 70+ irrespective of income.
ABDM (2021) issues the 14-digit ABHA digital health ID.
NHM = NRHM (2005) + NUHM (2013); ASHA workers are community health volunteers.
National Health Policy 2017 targets 2.5% of GDP on public health; AP scheme = Dr NTR Vaidya Seva (Aarogyasri).
items.source: PIB; National Health Authority; MoHFW; National Health Policy 2017

items.title: Eradication, elimination & WHO certifications
items.body:
**Eradication** = permanent global reduction to zero (only smallpox in humans). **Elimination** = reduction to zero (or below a threshold) in a defined area.

**Achieved in India:**

| Disease | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Smallpox | Globally eradicated 1980 (last India case 1975) |
| Guinea worm | Eliminated from India 2000 |
| Polio | India / WHO SEAR certified polio-free 2014 |
| Maternal & neonatal tetanus | Eliminated 2015 |
| Yaws | India first country validated 2016 |
| Trachoma | WHO-validated elimination 2024 |

**Ongoing elimination targets:** **tuberculosis by 2025** (five years ahead of the SDG 2030 target, via **TB Mukt Bharat** and Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana nutrition support), **kala-azar**, **measles-rubella**, and **lymphatic filariasis** (mass drug administration).

**Antimicrobial resistance (AMR)** — microbes evolving to resist drugs, worsened by antibiotic overuse in humans and livestock; India's **National Action Plan on AMR (2017)** and the **Red Line campaign** (prescription-only marking) address it under a **One Health** frame.
keyPoints: Smallpox is the only human disease eradicated globally (1980); guinea worm eliminated from India in 2000.
India/WHO SEAR certified polio-free in 2014; maternal & neonatal tetanus eliminated 2015.
India first country validated for yaws (2016); WHO validated trachoma elimination (2024).
TB elimination target = 2025 (ahead of SDG 2030) via TB Mukt Bharat & Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana.
AMR = drug resistance from antibiotic overuse; addressed by NAP-AMR (2017) & Red Line campaign.

items.title: Nutrition programmes & recent outbreaks
items.body:
**Nutrition & child-health programmes:**
- **POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018)** — overarching mission to cut stunting, wasting, anaemia and low birth weight (life-cycle approach); now under **Mission POSHAN 2.0 / Saksham Anganwadi**.
- **PM POSHAN (2021)** — the renamed Mid-Day Meal Scheme; hot cooked meals for school children.
- **Anaemia Mukt Bharat** — 6x6x6 strategy to reduce anaemia across life-cycle groups.
- **ICDS (1975)** — Anganwadi services for children under 6, pregnant and lactating mothers.

**Recent outbreaks / alerts (exam-relevant):**
- **Nipah** — recurring in Kerala; fruit-bat reservoir; high case-fatality; contained via containment zones + contact tracing.
- **Mpox (monkeypox)** — WHO declared a **Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024**.
- **HMPV (human metapneumovirus)** — respiratory virus that drew attention in early 2025.
- **COVID-19** — reinforced pandemic preparedness and the **One Health** approach (human-animal-environment).

Key institutions: **ICMR** (biomedical research), **CDSCO** (drug regulator), the **AIIMS** network.
keyPoints: POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018) fights malnutrition/stunting; PM POSHAN (2021) = renamed Mid-Day Meal.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat uses a 6x6x6 strategy; ICDS (1975) delivers Anganwadi services.
Nipah (fruit-bat reservoir) recurs in Kerala with high case-fatality.
WHO declared Mpox a PHEIC in August 2024; HMPV drew attention in early 2025.
ICMR = biomedical research; CDSCO = central drug regulator; One Health links human-animal-environment.
items.source: Ministry of Women & Child Development; WHO; MoHFW; PIB
